title: Psychological Operations Specialist, (PO Specialist)
raw_text:
10-37F. MOS 37F--Psychological Operations Specialist, (PO Specialist), CMF 37 (Effective
202511)
       a. Major duties. The Psychological Operations (PO) specialist conducts analysis of target
audiences and environments; advises commanders and staffs; plans influence activities;
develops series; conducts influence operations, and assesses progress towards approved
objectives in support of the five branch functions (Military Information Support Operations [MISO],
Psychological Warfare [PSYWAR], Build Partner Influence Capacity, Military Deception
(MILDEC), and Civil Authority Information Support [CAIS]) to create and reinforce desired
behaviors in selected foreign individuals and groups to achieve military and U.S. national
objectives across the range of military operations. Duties for military occupational specialty
(MOS) 37F at each level of skill are as follows:
       (1) MOSC 37F1O. (USAR Only) Trains and maintains proficiency in all major duties.
Research finished and current intelligence and open-source information Records, cross-
references, stores and retrieves information manually or using automated data processing
equipment. Develops concepts and designs product prototypes. Distributes and disseminates PO
products. Performs initial analysis of adversary propaganda products and other media.
Safeguards classified and sensitive material. Maintains journals, status boards, operations maps,
and overlays. Operates and maintains organic communications, production, and other equipment.
Prepares and presents briefings. Operates PO specific equipment.
       (2) MOSC 37F2O. Perform all duties of preceding skill level. Provides specific guidance
and training for subordinates. Identifies and maintains information on the availability of products
and delivery means. Determines the appropriate mix of media to implement PO. Supervises
packaging of PO products for delivery by various means. Evaluates the effectiveness of PO
products. Analyzes psychological vulnerabilities, and susceptibilities of PO target audiences to
determine potential for exploitation. Evaluates current intelligence, PO studies and estimates to
determine PO targets. Establishes and maintains reference files of translated materials. Analyzes
adversary propaganda and other media.
       (3) MOSC 37F3O. Perform all duties of preceding skill level. Provides specific guidance
and training for subordinates. Assists in preparing and conducting PO training programs. Plans
and organizes work schedules and assigns specific tasks in support of PO missions. Conducts
liaison with the supported unit staffs. Coordinates resource requirements for the development,
production and dissemination of PO products. Advises supported units on PO planning
considerations. Integrates PO into conventional and special operations tactical through strategic
level planning. Analyzes current intelligence products to identify gaps and subsequent collection
requirements to support PO. Supervises receipt, analysis, and storage of PO-related information.
Assists in the planning, identification and deployment of PO forces. Coordinates PO information
collection requirements with supported command. Reviews analysis performed by subordinates.
Supervises scriptwriters, broadcast specialists, journalists, and illustrators in the development and
production of PO products. Supervises PO distribution and dissemination of PO products.
Determines dissemination requirements for PO products. Assesses the overall impact of the PO
series on target audience behavior.
       (4) MOSC 37F4O. Perform all duties of preceding skill level. Provides specific guidance
and training for subordinates. Develops and conducts PO specific training programs. Plans and
organizes PO task organizations. Supervises the planning, production and dissemination of PO
products. Supervises the implementation and execution of PO. Coordinates PO liaison activities
within supporting and supported unit staffs. Assists in planning for PO units at Brigade Combat
Team (BCT) and above.
       (5) MOSC 37F5O. Perform all duties of preceding skill level. Provides specific guidance
and training for subordinates. Coordinates PO liaison activities within supporting and supported
unit staffs. Supervises the planning, organization, training, and coordination of activities within PO
units. Supervises the employment of PO forces and execution of PO activities. Conducts planning
for PO units at GCCs. Performs duties as PO staff NCO at Division and above, Command
headquarters and joint commands.
       (6) MOSC 37F6O. Perform all duties of preceding skill level. Advises the commander and
staff on all matters pertaining to enlisted personnel. Enforces the implementation of established
policies and standards as they pertain to enlisted personnel within the command. Provides
 counsel and guidance to the NCOs and other enlisted Soldiers of the command. Manages the
daily activities and operations of the unit.
        b. PO specialists must possess the following qualifications for training and initial award of
MOS 37:
             (1) A physical demands rating of significant (Gray). Active Component in-service
Soldiers who have successfully completed and have been selected from the PO Assessment and
Selection (POAS) Course will be awarded OPAT score of Significant.
             (2) A physical profile of 111221.
             (3) Normal color vision.
             (4) Must demonstrate clear enunciation and comprehension of English and good
Standard English grammar skills.
             (5) (AC Soldiers only) Must have a current Airborne physical exam and be able to meet
medical fitness standards as outlined in AR 40–501. Female Soldiers must have a negative
pregnancy test within 30 days of their PO Assessment and Selection Report date.
             (6) These qualifications may be waived with the written approval of the Command
Surgeon, U.S. Army John F. Kennedy Special Warfare Center and School (USAJFKSWCS)
(AOJK–PO).
             (7) Administrative qualifications and scores.
                  (a)A high school graduate or equivalent.
                  (b) A U.S. citizen. (nonwaivable)
                  (c) Must possess a valid motor vehicle license from any of the 50 states or US
territories either in photo ID or paper form in accordance with applicants issuing State or US
Territory law(s) or regulations in order to ship from entry station to basic combat training location.
                 (d) RA NPS applicants must be 18 years of age by ship date to Basic Training and
have not reached their 35th birthday prior to ship date.
             (8) A minimum score of 105 in aptitude area GT effective 1 July 2020.
             (9) A minimum security eligibility of secret is required to attend MOS training and
award the initial MOS. Must be eligible to obtain a top secret (SCI) security clearance to maintain
the MOS. RA Soldiers must hold a final top secret with sensitive compartmental information
security clearance within 24 months of initial MOS award. USAR Soldiers must have a top secret
when required by their position. If a Soldier is unable to obtain a favorable adjudication of their
security clearance after graduation of the PO training pathway they will be terminated from PO
duty, CMF 37 MOS withdrawn, and reported for immediate reclassification and assignment in
accordance with all applicable Army Regulations.
             (10) These qualifications may be waived with the written approval of the PO
Commandant, USAJFKSWCS (AOJK–PO).
             (11) Moral qualifications.
                   (a) No record of conviction by court-martial or have disciplinary action noted in
their Official Military Personnel File under the provisions of the UCMJ, Art. 15
                   (b) No record of civil conviction by a civil court for any offense other than minor
traffic violations.
                   (c) Not barred to reenlistment or under suspension of favorable personnel action
(see AR 600–8–2).
                   (d) Must not have any lost time under 10 USC 972 within the current or preceding
enlistment. Lost time more than 30 days is nonwaivable.
                   (e) AC Soldiers will be disqualified from attending POAS if they have engaged in
any conduct specifically prohibited by CG, USAJFKSWCS.
                   (f) These qualifications may be waived with the written approval of the PO
Commandant, USAJFKSWCS (AOJK–PO).
             (12) Formal training (All Soldiers).
                   (a) Must complete Basic Combat Training, Advanced Individual Training, or One
Station Unit Training.
                   (b) USAR Initial Entry Training Soldiers must complete the MOS 37F course
conducted under the auspices of the U.S. Army John F. Kennedy Special Warfare Center and
School.
             (13) Formal training (AC Soldiers only).
                 (a) Must be airborne-qualified or are qualified for and volunteer to attend airborne
training.
                (b) (NPS Soldiers only) Must complete the PO Preparatory and Conditioning
Course.
                (c) Must successfully complete and be selected from the POAS course.
                (d) Must successfully complete Basic Leaders Course (BLC), if not previously
qualified.
                  (e) Complete the MOS 37F PO Training Pathway (POTP) conducted under the
auspices of the USAJFKSWCS.
                  (f) Have a qualifying DLAB, DLPT, or OPI test score IAW AR 11-6 received 12
months prior to attending POAS.
                  (g) Must meet requirements IAW AR 614-200 for assignment to the AC.
            (14) Reclassification into MOS 37F.
                  (a) Must not be currently serving in a restricted MOS or Branch and are eligible to
reclassify from current MOS into CMF 37.
                  (b) Must meet requirements IAW AR 614-200 for assignment.
                  (c) (AC Soldiers only) Must be in grades E2/PV2 with a minimum of 12 months of
active federal service (AFS) through E5/SGT with no more than 8 years AFS at time of
submission of reclassification packet to attend the POAS course. Soldiers in grade E7/SFC are
not authorized to not attend the POTP.
                  (d) (USAR Soldiers only) Must be in grade E6/SSG and below.
                  (e) These qualifications may be waived with the written approval of the PO
Commandant, USAJFKSWCS (AOJK–PO).
            (15) The CMF 37 MOS is withdrawn if:
                  (a) SMs security clearance is revoked or not maintained IAW 10-37F, paragraph
2(g).
                  (b) Physical qualifications are lost and SMs are not found fit to perform CMF 37
MOS tasks by a medical evaluation board.
                  (c) SM has committed any act or engaged in conduct inconsistent with Special
Operations Forces core attributes or displays repeated substandard performance and conduct as
determined by the Soldier’s General Court Martial Convening Authority.
                  (d) They fail to fulfill professional requirements or are found unsuitable, as
evidenced by any of the following (not all inclusive):
             (1) Civil convictions for a felony offense or an offense involving moral turpitude or any
other conviction for civilian criminal offenses that result in suspended or unsuspended
punishments of more than 6 months confinement or a fine in excess of $5,000.
             (2) Initiation of any adverse administrative elimination action for reasons specified in
AR 635–200.
             (3) Repeated failure to perform MOS-related or ASI-related duties after counseling
and rehabilitative reassignment.
             (4) Any other act or series of acts inconsistent with the integrity, professionalism, and
conduct required of a PO Soldier.

    c Additional skill identifiers. (Refer to table 12-8 for (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with
all enlisted MOS)).
    d Position coding and personnel utilization restrictions.
          (1) Non-Career Recruiter (SQI 4). Position coding and personnel utilization not
              authorized except in the Special Operations Recruiting Battalion, Ft Liberty, NC.
          (2) Drill Sergeant (SQI X). Positions may be coded with SQI X and personnel utilized at
              U.S. Army Maneuver Support Center of Excellence and U.S. Army John F. Kennedy
              Special Warfare Center and School only.
    e Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to
each skill level are listed in the following tables:
          (3) Table 10-37F-1. Physical requirements.
          (4) Table 10-37F-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
          (5) Table 10-37F-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
